title: Two-Stage Op Amps and Gain Boosting
intro: When one stage cannot deliver enough gain and swing, a second stage is added. The price is stability work.

blocks.text: A differential pair with a mirror load drives a common-source second stage. Gain is the product of the two stage gains, gm1*(ro2||ro4) * gm6*(ro6||ro7), commonly 60 to 80 dB. The output can swing within an overdrive of each rail. A compensation capacitor CC around the second stage (Miller compensation) keeps it stable (see the next chapter).

blocks.alt: Block diagram of a two-stage op amp. The input drives the first stage, a differential stage, whose output drives the second, common-source stage and then the output. A compensation capacitor Cc connects from the output of the first stage to the output of the second.
blocks.caption: A two-stage op amp. The Miller capacitor Cc spans the second stage.

blocks.text: To get cascode-level output resistance without the swing penalty, add an auxiliary amplifier that regulates the cascode transistor's source, multiplying the output resistance by its gain. Gain boosting raises DC gain by 20 to 40 dB at the cost of more current and some extra poles.

items: The peak output swing is VDD minus the sum of overdrives of the transistors in series at each rail.
Fully differential op amps need common-mode feedback (CMFB): a circuit that senses the output common-mode level and corrects the load currents to hold it near a reference.

blocks.text: Large inputs saturate the differential pair; the output is then limited by how fast the tail current ISS can charge the compensation or load capacitor: SR = ISS/CC (two-stage, first stage limit) or ISS/CL (single stage). Slew rate causes distortion and sets settling time for large steps.

blocks.title: Two-stage gain
blocks.text: Stage one has gm1 = 1 mS with output resistance 50 kohm || 50 kohm. Stage two has gm6 = 2 mS with output resistance 25 kohm. Find the total gain.

blocks.title: Slewing
blocks.text: ISS = 100 uA, CC = 1 pF. A 0.5 V step is applied. How long does the output slew, and what is the slew rate?
solution: SR = ISS / CC = 100 uA / 1 pF = 100 V/us.
Time to slew 0.5 V = 0.5 V / (100 V/us) = 5 ns.
blocks.answer: SR = 100 V/us; 5 ns to slew 0.5 V.
